Digital fit scenario assessment — 2026-10-14

This is a model check against declared digital contexts, not a fit claim for an actual pan. The nominal proxy is the current editable reconstruction; the other four cases perturb one interface input at a time. Their offsets are design stress choices, not measured uncertainty bands or predicted manufacturing tolerances. Exact solid intersections are evaluated from the saved A/B/C STEP geometry. Every moving gate is checked from 0° through 60° in 5° steps plus the known nominal roof-critical angle; fixed geometry is checked once per context.

One-variable proxy sensitivity scans

Each scan changes one assumed pan parameter at a time and holds insert placement fixed. Exact saved BRep solids are checked against only the changed proxy surfaces at the declared gate samples (0–60° every 5°, plus 43.897886°). A coarse scan finds the first sampled hit; bisection then narrows the adjacent clear/hit interval to the listed resolution. This is a reproducible sampled bracket, not a guaranteed continuous global threshold: a narrow collision window between coarse probes may be missed. All ranges below are deliberately chosen digital probes, not measured dimensions or uncertainty bounds.

The displayed first-hit side uses exact Boolean volume above the validator's 1e-5 mm³ threshold. The nominal pan interior, cover shape, pickup and tube remain illustrative proxies. “No hit” means only that none was detected at the scan's coarse probe values through its endpoint; it does not establish a physical clearance margin. Raw values, pair identity, interval, resolution, source hashes and all sampled angles are recorded in validation.json and shown with the live site cards.

Installation and withdrawal paths

The saved closed-door assembly is translated vertically at its installed XY/yaw placement, with the cover removed. Exact BRep overlap is checked every 1 mm until the insert bottom is 1 mm above the proxy pan rim. The tube-present route includes the pickup keep-out and tube; the alternate route omits both together as a hypothetical complete pickup/suction-pipe assembly removal. The screen is not separated from the pipe in this check.

This shows that a simple straight withdrawal is blocked by the retained tube proxy under the nominal arrangement, while a conditional path exists in four contexts if the complete pickup/tube assembly is absent. That is a digital sequence hypothesis, not a Solstice service instruction: mount access, suction-pipe removal/reinstallation, exact tube geometry, door motion during handling and continuous motion are not established. Exact per-concept and per-context first-hit records are in validation.json under installation_paths.

Eight alternative routes are also checked per concept against the nominal pan shell and fixed pickup/tube proxy, with the cover removed and doors closed. Four translate ±20 mm along X or Y, then lift; four tilt ±5° about X or Y, then lift. Translations are sampled every 1 mm and rotations every 1°. Tilts rotate about each insert's assembled bounding-box centre. A first collision is reported at a sampled pose; this is not a continuous swept-volume proof.

All 24 selected routes encounter a modeled proxy at a sampled pose. The X-shift and tilt cases meet the proxy during their first motion stage; the listed Y-shift cases meet it during the shift or the subsequent lift as shown. This says only that these specific routes do not clear this nominal reconstruction. It does not establish that all removal paths are blocked, because the hidden pan interior and tube coordinates remain uncertain and the route set is deliberately finite. Exact sampled positions and overlap volumes are in validation.json under digital_alternative_exit_path_study.

Gate gravity-direction sensitivity

The saved moving solids were sampled at each declared gate angle. Their volume-weighted centroids, transformed hinge pivots and axes, and effective-gravity vectors give the signed static gravity torque per kilogram. Positive torque follows increasing gate angle toward the 60° stop; negative torque tends toward closed. Pins are excluded because they are fixed in this kinematic model. The report stores each gate's full torque curve in validation.json under gravity_torque_study.

At level, every gate has the same modeled closing bias, −0.019261979 N·m/kg. The direction-dependent open biases show that gate count and orientation change the static response. The pan axes have not been registered to the installed car, so these are deliberately selected sensitivity directions, not vehicle attitudes or cornering limits. The calculation excludes oil, hinge friction, surface adhesion, impacts and opening time; it cannot predict when a gate will move in service.

Interpretation and limits

The result ranks sensitivity to this scenario set, not physical fit or oil-control performance. In particular, the 25% pickup change and route offset are not claims about the OEM strainer or tube; the narrow shell is not a reconstructed casting tolerance. The radial result only means its saved geometry has no Boolean intersection with these five modeled contexts at the stated samples.

The path checks sample straight, shifted and tilted translations only. They do not prove a continuous swept volume, open-door handling, installed orientation, service-tool access or tolerance/deflection margin. The published GM overall dimensions constrain only the pan outside envelope; its hidden cavity and fit interfaces remain unknown. Official 12601240 photos add qualitative exact-part topology; Vue service figures are application-unresolved or an LY7/12666374 analog and add no target dimensions. See `same-pan-family-visuals.md`.
